title: Challenge: BMI Calculator Solution
summary: Walkthrough of the BMI calculator function: first verify the formula by hand, then build bmiCalculator(weight, height), then refine it with Math.pow and Math.round.

concepts.heading: Plan the maths before the code
points: BMI = weight in kg divided by height in metres squared. Work an example on a calculator first (65 kg, 1.8 m: 1.8 x 1.8 = 3.24, 65 / 3.24 is about 20.06) so you know what the function should output.
The challenge's starter code (variables plus a console.log call) is pasted into a DevTools Snippet, and the function is written beneath it.

concepts.heading: Building the function
points: Start with the function keyword, then the exact name required by the tests (bmiCalculator), then parentheses holding the inputs in the required order: weight first, height second.
Inside the curly braces compute bmi = weight / (height * height). The brackets force the multiplication to be evaluated first; without them division would happen first and the result would be wrong.
Use the return keyword to hand the value back to the caller. Without return the function gives back undefined.
Paste into the exercise's test runner and press Check solution to confirm it passes.

concepts.heading: Refinement 1: Math.pow
points: Math.pow(base, exponent) raises a number to a power, so Math.pow(height, 2) replaces height * height. Same result, slightly tidier.
The method was found by searching the web ('raise a number to a power javascript') and reading the MDN page. Looking things up like this is a normal part of programming.

concepts.heading: Refinement 2: Math.round
points: Raw output has many decimal places (about 20.0672839...). BMI is normally shown as a whole number.
Math.round(x) returns the nearest integer: 2.5 and above rounds up to 3, 2.4 rounds to 2. Math.floor always rounds down, so round is the more accurate choice here.
Change the return line to return Math.round(bmi). With 65 and 1.8 the output is 20, and the test suite still passes.
(Extra) Math.ceil rounds up and toFixed(n) returns a string with n decimals; neither is needed here.

concepts.heading: What comes next
points: The following section covers control flow, which is how this BMI function will later be extended to interpret the number.

task.name: BMI calculator function (solution)
task.starting_point: Starter code declaring weight and height variables and logging the result of bmiCalculator, with the function left to write.
task.goal: Define bmiCalculator(weight, height) that returns the BMI as a whole number.
steps: Work an example by hand to know the expected value.
Write function bmiCalculator(weight, height) { ... } with inputs in that order.
Compute bmi = weight / (height * height), keeping the brackets.
Return bmi, then check against the tests.
Return Math.round(bmi) to get a whole number.
task.expected_result: bmiCalculator(65, 1.8) returns 20 and the check passes.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 14 - Introduction to Javascript ES6/14.15 - Challenge - Create a BMI Calculator/script.js

pitfalls: Writing weight / height * height: it evaluates left to right and cancels out.
Forgetting return, so the function yields undefined.
Putting parameters in the wrong order (height, weight).
Using Math.floor when nearest rounding is wanted.

playground.coverage: Covers the task, brackets pitfall, Math.round vs floor/ceil/toFixed and a ** variant.
gaps_and_ideas: Add a Math.pow(height, 2) variant since the lecture shows it.
Add a 'work it out on paper first' step with the 65 / 1.8 example.
Interactive demo idea: sliders for weight and height showing the unrounded and rounded BMI.
